P1.evidence: No setter notes read back — in fact the prospect could not remember the setter's name and the rep supplied it ('Kim?') without using anything from the call. The frame was the closest to complete in this batch, three parts of four: 'understand what exactly is going on with your fitness right now, what's working, what's not, what are you looking to accomplish' — where you are, what's in the way and where you want to go, missing only what you need. But no frame agreement was sought at all; there was no 'does that work?' and the rep simply continued. Opening question ran clean: 'what would you say in your opinion is maybe the biggest challenge that you're having with your fitness right now?'

P2.evidence: The only clean P2b in the batch — 'What do you do for work? Is it active? You're sedentary?' asked exactly as scripted, producing quality engineer, desk-bound, roughly 3,000 steps. Sleep and energy both properly run for the first time in this batch: the sleep question surfaced apnoea, snoring, morning headaches and non-restorative sleep, and 'How are your energy levels, like, throughout the day? Have they ever changed at all?' surfaced the sluggishness and the planned hormone panel. Training week was covered in unusual detail, right down to the daily schedule from a 4am wake to a 9pm bed. Against that, age and weight were both volunteered rather than asked and no height or absolute weight was ever established. Injuries were surfaced by a good question — 'Do you have any pain in those areas?' — which produced a Bankart shoulder fracture and recurrent sciatica, and then dropped instantly: the rep said only 'Okay, got it. So you got the shoulder injury, tightness in the back and legs' and changed subject. No severity, no current limitation, no duration, no follow-up ever. Diet never asked.

P3.evidence: The surface layer ran and the deep layer never started. 'When you said that you like let yourself go, is there any places in particular that you're talking about?' produced the weight and muscle loss, and mobility, strength and energy were all canvassed. From there nothing. No 'something you want to do but can't', no 'when you're moving better what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact', and no drive through to family, identity or legacy. The children came from the prospect unprompted and were left where they landed: 'you want to be able to keep up with them and be mobile and be able to play really hard with them. And I got two boys.' The prospect also handed over the most emotionally loaded line of the batch — 'not to blame my kid, but if I didn't have the kid, then I would probably still be active' — and it drew no response at all. The closing summary was a recap, not a tie-down.

P4.evidence: The best phase on the call and the one that produced the real objection. 'Have you ever worked with anyone, maybe like us, or like a personal trainer, or have you always been a do-it-yourself type of guy?' produced the full history: a thousand videos, bought bodybuilding plans, free plans from bodybuilder.com, and an informal friend who became a coach. The blocker question was then asked directly — 'what is the reason why you would not just go back to what you were doing before, researching yourself? Is it just the time of putting it all together?' — and it flushed out the actual objection, which was fear of the coaching format rather than time. The prospect named his own gap unprompted and precisely: 'Structure, I would say structure and movement.' Marked down only because the streak-and-collapse pattern was volunteered rather than asked for, and it is the single most diagnostic thing he said.

P5.evidence: Absent for the fifth consecutive call in this batch. The prospect delivered the two-year question himself and it was left on the table: 'I'm kind of a guy that goes through streaks... I'll have like six months of really dedicated and then I'll fall off for a couple months... But as time has gone on, I've gone through longer and longer and longer stretches.' Combined with 20 pounds gained in eight months, worsening sleep apnoea tied to that weight, a sedentary job and two children under three, the cost of inaction was fully assembled and never once named.

P6.evidence: The nearest thing to a belief check was the rep asserting fit and asking for agreement — 'I think what we're doing would probably make sense for you, but I guess, what are your thoughts?' → 'No, I would agree, definitely' — which is a fit check rather than the scripted 'do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner?'. The all-in question never ran. And P6c was inverted: when hesitation surfaced, the script requires returning to Phase 5, and the rep instead moved down-market to a cheaper product, which resolved nothing and removed the flagship from the conversation permanently.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, but only on the secondary product: after quoting Primal University at $199 a month the rep asked 'any questions about what's included or where do you want go from here?'. No payment was requested and no link was sent. Steps two to four relate to Kettlebell Body onboarding and could not apply, since the flagship was never priced or offered — it was described only as 'obviously in the thousands'.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest fear trigger in the batch and the clearest miss. The prospect said 'as far as coaching, I don't know if I'm ready to go that far. I haven't done it, so there's hesitation there', and the rep asked the ideal opening question — 'Where does the hesitation come from?' — receiving 'I've just never done it. And as far as paying for it and doing videos and sending it to people, I've just never done anything like that.' That is textbook first-time fear, and the play has a move written for precisely it: 'BRIDGE: I'm not asking you to see the whole other side, just take the first step.' Nothing ran. No certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain frame, no bridge, no plane, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. The rep answered a fear objection with a cheaper product.

Trigger present at the end — 'I guess I'll just have to kind of think about investing that much' and 'I was just more or less checking it out'. Not a single move ran. The rep's entire response was to disposition the call himself: 'So I guess we'll just call it a no for now, then.'

Money surfaced against the $199 monthly figure and drew no response whatsoever — no isolate, no should-I-versus-how frame, no financial picture, no attempt to establish whether $199 was genuinely the barrier or a proxy for the unresolved fear objection from ten minutes earlier.

Script gap: a prospect who wants the artifact rather than the relationship. He said it plainly three times — 'I was kind of like looking for a plan with you, with like Trevor, like looking to see if he had a plan', 'it'd be nice to actually do a nice plan', and 'get the plan, get access to the inventory would be the best'. The playbook has no path for converting someone who wants a programme into someone who wants coaching, and the commercial answer offered was simply to sell him the cheaper product he had already priced against free alternatives.

notes: Strong mechanical discovery — the only call in the batch to run work, sleep and energy properly — attached to no depth and no consequence frame, so when the fear objection arrived there was nothing behind it. The correctable moment is exact and single: at 00:26:21 the rep had the objection isolated and named, and needed the bridge move, not a $199 alternative. Present one offer, resolve the fear, and only then discuss format.
